rics.description: Foreign currency reserves, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
rics.meaning: Foreign currency reserves YoY % change, standardized.
rics.how_to_use: Most useful for cross-country comparison. US reserves are tiny relative to GDP because USD is reserve currency — focus on the trend, not the level.

rics.description: Official international reserves, % month on month, Standardized, Chg P/P
rics.meaning: Official international reserves MoM % change, standardized.
rics.how_to_use: Watch for unusual swings — large MoM moves can signal FX intervention or valuation effects from gold/SDR repricing.

rics.description: Official international reserves, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
rics.meaning: Official international reserves YoY % change, standardized.
rics.how_to_use: Cleaner trend signal than MoM. US reserves grow mostly through gold revaluation and IMF position changes; FX trading is rare.
Sum of FX, gold, SDR, IMF reserve position. Used for FX intervention capacity (rarely deployed for the US).

rics.meaning: Reserve Assets (total) — US international reserves: gold, foreign currency holdings, IMF position, SDRs. ~$700B total.
rics.how_to_use: Small relative to US GDP (~3%) — US is reserve issuer, not reserve holder. Track for FX intervention capacity (rarely used post-1985). ~80% of total is gold (revaluation gain over decades).

rics.meaning: Foreign currency component of reserve assets — euros, yen, gold-backed.
rics.how_to_use: Smallest piece of US reserves. Big country FX reserves are mostly USD; the US holds mostly gold.

rics.meaning: Gold stock component of reserve assets, valued at official rate (~$42/oz historically — way below market).
rics.how_to_use: The US holds ~8,100 tonnes — largest in the world. Valued at the legacy book price, vastly understated. Market value is 30x+ book.

rics.description: Reserve Assets, Holdings of Special Drawing Rights
rics.meaning: Holdings of Special Drawing Rights at the IMF.
rics.how_to_use: SDRs are an IMF reserve unit. US allocation grew sharply in the 2021 SDR allocation post-COVID.

rics.description: Reserve Assets, Reserve position in IMF
rics.meaning: US reserve position in IMF — quota subscription minus IMF holdings of US currency.
rics.how_to_use: Mostly accounting. Moves when the US lends to IMF programs or its quota changes.

rics.meaning: US Foreign Reserves: Total Assets — same conceptual measure as aUSRES. Treasury monthly release.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check against aUSRES. The US holds reserves only minimally — most reserve-currency-issuer status means foreign central banks hold dollars instead.

rics.meaning: US Foreign Reserves: Gold — Treasury's gold holdings (~261M troy oz / ~8,134 metric tons). Largest national gold holding globally. Valued at ~$42/oz on books but market value far higher.
rics.how_to_use: Stock unchanged since 1970s. Book value uses 1973 statutory price ($42/oz); market value 50× higher. Recent gold rally has put 'unrealized' gains on US balance sheet at trillions — periodically discussed for revaluation.

rics.meaning: US Foreign Reserves: IMF Position — US reserve tranche position at the IMF. Funds the US can withdraw on demand from IMF without conditions.
rics.how_to_use: Small (~$50B). Used in BoP accounting; rarely activated. Tracks IMF financial commitments.

rics.meaning: US Foreign Reserves: Special Drawing Rights — SDR holdings at the IMF. International reserve asset created by IMF, valued by basket of major currencies.
rics.how_to_use: Boosted in 2021 IMF general allocation ($650B globally to support COVID recovery). Useful for tracking IMF reserve operations. Less liquid than Treasury foreign currency holdings.
